authority.name: City of Madison Building Inspection Division (Dept. of Planning & Community & Economic Development)

codeEdition.text: Madison's Development Services Center directs 1- and 2-family alteration work to the state code, Wis. Admin. Code chs. SPS 320-325 (Wisconsin Uniform Dwelling Code); any building with three or more attached units is handled under the commercial building code instead.

permitPolicy.text: An owner-occupant altering their own single-family home may pull both the building permit and the mechanical permits (plumbing, electrical, HVAC). An owner-occupant building a new house may pull only the building permit, and a non-occupant owner of a 1- or 2-family rental needs licensed professionals for both building and mechanical permits.

codeItems.text: Madison's smoke alarm ordinance reaches every residential building, including owner-occupied single-family homes: alarms must be hardwired with battery backup or powered by a sealed, non-removable 10-year battery, and no alarm may stay in service longer than ten years unless the manufacturer allows it.

Placement is stricter than the usual one-per-floor rule: an alarm is required in each bedroom, in each sleeping area, within six feet of every door leading to a bedroom or sleeping area, and on each floor of the building.

Electrical permits are counted by "openings" - outlets, switches, fixtures, junction boxes, subpanels and fixed appliances all count - and a service panel replacement is counted and priced separately from openings.
Water heaters and water softeners are named in the scope of the city's plumbing repair/replace permit, and plumbing permit fees are calculated from the number of new or replaced fixtures.

Moving or adding a permanent fixture (toilet, sink, shower, island or counter) pushes the job out of the over-the-counter permit and into plan review, so a relocated water heater or sink is not a same-day permit in Madison.

Connecting to, installing or replacing a water service requires a separate Water Utility application signed by a master plumber (and by the property owner for a new or replacement service), submitted with fees before work starts.

water-heater-replacement.requirement: Replacing a water heater needs a Madison plumbing permit; the city's plumbing data sheet is the application for water heater and softener replacements and prices the permit by fixture.

plumber-service-call.requirement: Plumbing work that adds or moves a fixture needs a plumbing permit from Building Inspection, priced per fixture with a minimum fee; jobs that do not require plan review can be applied for over the counter or online.

electrician-service-call.requirement: Electrical work in an existing building needs an electrical permit, priced by the number of openings added or moved, with a separate charge for replacing a service panel.
electrician-service-call.fee: $25.00 for openings 1-10 + $1.00 per additional opening; $50.00 per service panel

smoke-detector-replacement.requirement: Madison does not treat smoke alarms as a permit item, but its ordinance sets what you may install: a hardwired alarm with battery backup or a sealed 10-year-battery alarm, in each bedroom and sleeping area, within six feet of each bedroom door and on every floor, replaced at ten years.
